name: Jehoshaphat
description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Jehoshaphat is not moved by four hundred prophets speaking the same thing, and asks whether there is not yet a prophet of the Lord that they may inquire of him. He wants to hear from a true prophet of the Most High, not from prophets who serve the king.

Ahab answers that there is one man, Micaiah the son of Imlah, but he hates him because Micaiah does not prophesy good concerning him, but evil. Jehoshaphat rebukes him, saying, let not the king say so.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: The king of Israel calls an officer to hasten Micaiah, while Ahab and Jehoshaphat sit each on his throne in their robes at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets prophesy before them.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: Jehoshaphat makes peace with the king of Israel and puts the remnant of the sodomites out of the land. There is then no king in Edom but a deputy, because Edom had been subdued and had not yet revolted.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: Jehoram the son of Ahab begins to reign over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah and reigns twelve years. He works evil in the sight of the Lord, but not like his father and mother, for he puts away the image of Baal that his father had made.

note.label: 2 Kings 3: Three Kings and the Water in the Ditches

points: King Jehoram goes out of Samaria, numbers all Israel, and sends to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, telling him Moab has rebelled and asking whether he will go up with him to battle. Jehoshaphat answers, I will go up; I am as thou art, my people as thy people, and my horses as thy horses.

note.label: 2 Kings 3: Three Kings and the Water in the Ditches

points: Jehoshaphat asks whether there is not a prophet of the Lord that they may inquire of the Lord by him. One of the king of Israel's servants answers that Elisha the son of Shaphat is there, who poured water on the hands of Elijah.

note.label: 2 Kings 3: Three Kings and the Water in the Ditches

points: Jehoshaphat says the word of the Lord is with him, so the three kings go down to Elisha.

note.label: 2 Kings 3: Three Kings and the Water in the Ditches

points: Elisha says, as the Lord of hosts liveth before whom I stand, that were it not that he regarded the presence of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, he would not look toward the king of Israel nor see him. He addresses the matter only for the sake of the righteous king of Judah.

note.label: 2 Kings 3: Three Kings and the Water in the Ditches

points: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the kings of Israel because the daughter of Ahab was his wife.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: The kings of Judah are set down in order from Solomon: Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, Jehoshaphat, and on through the line.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 3: The Sons of David and the Kings of Judah

points: Jehoshaphat reigned in the place of his father Asa, taking the throne after him.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

points: The Most High was with Jehoshaphat because he walked in the first ways of his father David and sought not unto Baal.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

points: The fear of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms round about Judah so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

points: Jehoshaphat waxed great exceedingly and built castles and cities of store in Judah.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

points: Jehoshaphat had riches and honor and abundance, and joined affinity with Ahab through marriage.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 18: Jehoshaphat, Ahab, and the True Prophet

points: Ahab feasted him and persuaded him to go up to Ramoth Gilead, and Jehoshaphat answered, I am as thou art, my people as thy people, we will be with thee in the war.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 18: Jehoshaphat, Ahab, and the True Prophet

points: Jehoshaphat asked to inquire at the word of the Lord before going to battle.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 18: Jehoshaphat, Ahab, and the True Prophet

points: Jehoshaphat asked if there was not still a prophet of the Lord to inquire of.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 18: Jehoshaphat, Ahab, and the True Prophet

points: Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet Jehoshaphat and said, shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the Lord? Therefore is wrath upon thee from before the Lord. We got to be careful not to bring wrath upon us. We got to be careful not to bring wrath upon the congregation. The Lord does not like that thing right there.

note.label: Perilous Times: Judges and Soldiers

points: Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, joined himself with Ahaziah, king of Israel, who did very wickedly. Then Eliezer prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, because thou hast joined thyself with Ahaziah, the Lord hath broken thy works. And listen, we doing mighty works: all praises for good leadership, all praises for our bishops, our deacons, all praises for those who labor in Christ before us. But it's telling you that if we join with those who doing wickedness, the Lord will break our works. And the ships were broken, that they were not able to go to Tarshish.

note.label: Perilous Times: Judges and Soldiers

points: Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, and Jehoram his son reigned in his stead.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 21: Jehoram's Wicked Reign

points: There came a writing to Jehoram from Elijah the prophet, telling him he had not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat his father nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah, but in the way of the kings of Israel.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 21: Jehoram's Wicked Reign

points: They buried Ahaziah for the sake of Jehoshaphat his forefather who sought the Most High with all his heart; but the house of Ahaziah had no power to keep the kingdom, so the wicked king was cut off by the same hand the Most High anointed to avenge Israel.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 22: Ahaziah and the Rise of Athaliah

cases.name: Jehoshaphat
cases.charge: Walking in the first ways of his father David and seeking not unto Baalim; sending princes and Levites with the book of the law to teach in all the cities of Judah; and setting singers before the army
cases.preview: The Lord was with Jehoshaphat because he walked in the first ways of David and did not seek Baal;

cases.name: Jehoshaphat’s alliances
cases.charge: Joining affinity with Ahab and going up with him to Ramoth-gilead against the word of the prophet; joining himself with Ahaziah to make ships
cases.preview: Jehoshaphat, who sought the Lord and taught the law through Judah, joined affinity with Ahab by marrying his son to Ahab’s daughter, and went up with him to Ramoth-gilead after the true prophet…
